title: Additional Help for Costly Medical Tests
what_it_is: Additional Help for Costly Medical Tests

sections.label: Outpatient scan subsidies and MediSave
sections.summary: Pioneers get 50% off subsidised bills; subsidies cover outpatient diagnostic scans and blood tests, and MediSave withdrawal limits apply for scans and elderly outpatient treatments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Pioneers enjoy a further 50% off the subsidised bill.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: These subsidies apply to outpatient diagnostic services needed for treatment, including magnetic resonance imaging (MRIs), computed tomography (CT) scans and blood tests.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Based on 2015 data, the median post-subsidy bill size for MRI was $260 while the 90th percentile bill size was $560.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: For CT scans, the median and 90th percentile post-subsidy bill sizes were $140 and $440 respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Besides Government subsidies, Singaporeans can use MediSave for outpatient scans, with a withdrawal limit of $300 per year for non-cancer scans and $600 per year for cancer scans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Elderly Singaporeans who are 65 years old and above also have the flexibility to use up to $200 of MediSave every year to pay for their outpatient treatments at public healthcare institutions and participating Community Health Assist Scheme general practitioner clinics.

sections.label: MediShield Life, MediSave, MediFund support
sections.summary: Singaporeans can claim up to $3,000 of MediShield Life and withdraw up to $1,200 MediSave monthly for chemotherapy, while low-income Singaporeans can apply for MediFund.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: For example, Singaporeans can claim up to $3,000 of MediShield Life, and withdraw up to $1,200 MediSave per month for their chemotherapy treatment, including diagnostic scans and investigations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Beyond Government subsidies, MediSave and MediShield Life, low-income Singaporeans who require further financial support can approach medical social workers at our public healthcare institutions to apply for MediFund.
